G.A.M.E. B.R.I.D.G.E. — User Manual

GameBridge v1.1.0 · English master manual

What is GameBridge?
GameBridge is middleware between a human, a local AI runtime and an external application. It provides controlled communication and interaction channels, while plugins/adapters define how a specific application is accessed. GameBridge itself is not the AI and is not an autonomous agent.

1. The Control Panel

The image below is the main visual map of the GameBridge control panel. Every numbered marker points to a button, switch, selector, control area or window control that a user may interact with.

GameBridge v1.1.0 — annotated control panel.

1.1 Status and AI controls

1 — Status

Shows the current GameBridge runtime status. This gives you a quick indication of whether the platform is ready, loading or otherwise occupied.

2 — AI Active

Enables or disables the active AI runtime. The selected model is not useful for interaction until the AI runtime is active.

3 — Internet AI

Controls the optional internet/online AI path when such a provider is configured. The current v1.1.0 setup primarily uses local Ollama models.

4 — Model selector

Selects the AI model currently used by GameBridge. In the v1.1.0 baseline this list is populated from the available Ollama models.

5 — Adapter selector

Selects the application adapter/plugin that GameBridge should use. If no adapter is loaded, Channel 2 application interaction is not available.

6 — Start / Connect Target

Starts or attaches to the selected application through its adapter. The exact behaviour depends on the plugin. For example, an adapter may attach to an already running application or launch it when appropriate.

1.2 Channels and interaction controls

7 — Channel 1: Text Chat

Enables the human-to-AI/GameBridge chat channel. This is the normal conversational path for sending requests and receiving responses.

8 — Voice Mode

Controls voice input/output functionality and the available voice profile controls. The exact available options depend on the configured voice components.

9 — Read Telemetry

Requests application state information from the active adapter. Telemetry is intentionally request-driven rather than a permanent background polling stream.

10 — Write to Adapter: Channel 2

Enables controlled interaction with the selected application. Channel 2 actions are defined by the active adapter/plugin.

Important: Channel 2 is not a general-purpose automation system. The adapter defines which interactions are available, and GameBridge controls whether those interactions are permitted.

1.3 Main window and chat controls

11 — System messages

The system/log area displays runtime information, status changes and other messages generated by GameBridge.

12 — Main display area

The central display area is the main visual workspace. Depending on the current state and configuration it can display application, interaction or other GameBridge content.

13 — Message input

Enter a message or request for Channel 1 here.

14 — Send

Sends the current Channel 1 message to the active AI interaction flow.

15 — Always on top

Keeps the GameBridge window above other application windows when enabled.

16 — Large text

Increases interface text size for easier reading.

17 — Dark text / text visibility control

Adjusts the text presentation option shown in the lower control area. This is useful when the interface needs a different text contrast.

18 — K2 Monitor

Enables the Channel 2 monitoring view used while application interaction is active.

22 — Settings

Opens the application's settings/options area.

23 — Window controls

Standard Windows controls for minimizing, maximizing/restoring and closing the GameBridge window.

2. Basic Startup

  1. Start GameBridge.
  2. Check the status indicator.
  3. Enable AI Active if you want to use an AI model.
  4. Select the desired model.
  5. Select an adapter/plugin if application interaction is required.
  6. Use Start / Connect Target to attach to or start the target application.
  7. Enable only the channels you actually need.
Simple rule: Channel 1 is communication. Channel 2 is application interaction. Telemetry is application-state readback requested when needed.

3. Using a Plugin / Adapter

GameBridge does not contain application-specific interaction logic in its core. Instead, an adapter/plugin provides the bridge between GameBridge and the target application.

For example, a plugin can define how GameBridge connects to an application, which actions are available and how application state can be read back.

Typical workflow

  1. Select the plugin in the adapter selector.
  2. Start or attach to the target application.
  3. Enable the required interaction channel.
  4. Use Channel 1 to communicate with the AI.
  5. Allow Channel 2 only when application interaction is intended.
  6. Use telemetry/readback when application state needs to be observed.

4. AI Models

The v1.1.0 baseline uses Ollama as its current local AI provider. The model selector therefore shows models available through the local Ollama setup. Different models can behave differently even when they receive the same GameBridge tools and instructions.

A smaller model may understand simple interactions but struggle with longer multi-step tasks. A different model may interpret the same tool description in a different way. This is a model capability difference, not necessarily a GameBridge or plugin failure.

Important architectural note: Ollama is the current AI provider, not the definition of GameBridge itself. GameBridge's interaction and plugin architecture is intended to remain independent of the particular AI provider used.

5. Localization

GameBridge supports localized interface text through the locale configuration file: 

config/locales.json

The locale file contains the translated strings used by the interface. If you want to change the available language or modify a translation, edit the appropriate entries in this file.

Changing or adding translations

  1. Open the GameBridge installation/project directory.
  2. Open config/locales.json.
  3. Locate the language section you want to edit.
  4. Change the corresponding text values.
  5. Save the file.
  6. Restart GameBridge if necessary for the changes to be loaded.

Keep the JSON structure intact when editing the file. Translation keys are used by the application to find the correct text, so changing a key name can break the corresponding interface text.

6. Voice and Hotkey

Voice input can be enabled through the voice controls in the interface. The configured voice hotkey is stored in GameBridge's configuration and can be used to activate the voice interaction workflow.

The exact available voice behaviour depends on the installed/configured voice components and the current runtime state.

7. Telemetry

Telemetry is deliberately separate from Channel 2 interaction. Telemetry is used to request information from an active adapter, while Channel 2 is used to perform an interaction defined by that adapter.

This separation means that reading application state does not automatically mean that GameBridge is allowed to modify the application.

8. Troubleshooting

No adapter is loaded

Check that the plugin exists in the GameBridge plugin directory and that its adapter is discoverable. Then restart or refresh the runtime as appropriate.

Channel 2 does nothing

Check that an adapter is selected, the target application is connected and Channel 2 is enabled. The active plugin determines which actions are actually supported.

The AI behaves differently between models

This is expected. Models differ in tool interpretation, context handling and multi-step reasoning. Test the same GameBridge workflow with another model before assuming that the plugin or runtime is broken.

A duplicate plugin warning appears

GameBridge can detect a situation where an unpacked plugin and a .gbp package are present in the same plugin directory. Keep only the intended representation and restart GameBridge.

9. Configuration Overview

GameBridge keeps application configuration and localized interface data separate from the core runtime. Plugin-specific configuration can likewise remain outside the plugin implementation where supported by the plugin format.

For normal users, the most relevant configuration locations are:

  • config/locales.json — interface translations and localized text.
  • plugins/ — installed/unpacked plugins and adapters.
  • .env — environment-specific configuration where applicable.

10. Design Principle

GameBridge is the bridge.
The AI decides what it wants to request. GameBridge routes and controls the interaction. The adapter knows how to communicate with the target application. The target application remains outside GameBridge.

This separation is what allows the same GameBridge runtime to work with very different applications without embedding every application's behaviour into the core.
